assumptions: One server-generated immutable document ID, complete content with two fragments, two already resolved request scopes, and one primary write transaction at a time. UUID reuse and document replacement are outside this model.

Document and fragment publication or deletion commit atomically. Rollback preserves every previously committed row. PostgreSQL transaction isolation and the parent row lock are assumed; general TypeScript/SQL refinement is not proved.

The caller has authenticated and resolved the scope. This model does not prove authentication, account deletion fencing, R2 upload/cleanup, SSRF, indexing consumers, arbitrary text bytes or multi-document request atomicity.

Real PGlite tests exercise complete text and retained metadata, rollback after a prior fragment batch, throwing/suppressed parent deletion failures, HTTP deletion and foreign-scope refusal. They do not establish the full PostgreSQL lock graph.
bounds.progress: Pending database transactions settle only under weak fairness of their commit/rollback continuations. No provider, scheduler or network availability is assumed.

assumptions: The pending primary transaction eventually returns or rolls back, modeled by weak fairness of finish. This does not promise successful publication or deletion.
